About Us

🎯

Our Mission

The Jamaica Practical Nurses Alliance's mission is to provide compassionate, patient-centered care that upholds dignity, promotes healing, and empowers individuals to live healthier lives. As a united team of nurses, we are committed to continuous learning, seeking new healthcare interventions, and advocating for the well-being of our patients, members, and communities.

🌟

Our Vision

To be recognized as a trusted and dynamic nursing team that uplifts lives through empathy, expertise, and a relentless commitment to advancing healthcare.

💡

Our Philosophy

The Practical Nurses Association of Jamaica endeavours to promote our members through:

  • Registration
  • Planning
  • Participating in and initiating in researching through continuing education
📰

Our Story & Overview

The Practical Nurses Association of Jamaica (PNAJ) was founded on April 17, 1990 out of concern by Mr. Neville Atkinson (deceased), who was not a nurse but a civil servant. After a visit to a nursing home to pray with some patients, he was confronted by a group of Practical Nurses who approached him with "Tales of Woes" about the injustice that was meted out to them by their employer(s). He then went to the National Workers' Union (NWU) to seek representational rights for these nurses, and the Practical Nurses Association became affiliated to the Union.

The association grew and was facilitated with an office space, using the auditorium at the Workers' Union for monthly meetings. Over the years the association held various meetings with government officials. The existence of the association seeks to: represent the interest of practical nurses in Jamaica; establish a national curriculum for all nursery schools; ensure the sitting of a national examination for all nurses; and ensure practical nurses are trained to the highest standard.

We are also proud members of St. John's Ambulance, Red Cross, Ostomy Welfare Group and B.A.S.E. Foundation (Better Awareness & Support for Endometriosis). We are now proudly registered since May 6, 2025 under the name Jamaica Practical Nurses Alliance — and we are here today, doing our best to educate all our members to the highest standard.
